config.title: Inline Styles

intro.title: Inline Styles
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays a styled greeting message. You will learn how to apply inline styles directly within your component's HTML template using Angular's style binding syntax. The core concept involves dynamically setting CSS properties on HTML elements through TypeScript expressions in your template. You'll work with Angular's template syntax, style bindings, and basic TypeScript to control visual appearance directly from the component logic.
intro.usecase: Inline styles in Angular are commonly used for dynamic UI adjustments where styles need to change based on user interactions or data values. For example, in dashboard applications, developers use inline styles to highlight data points with conditional colors—like turning a metric red when it exceeds a threshold. In interactive components such as progress bars or sliders, inline styles dynamically update width or position based on real-time values. This approach is also practical for quick prototyping or applying one-off visual tweaks without creating separate CSS classes.

objectives: Apply inline styles to Angular components using the style attribute
Configure dynamic style bindings with Angular property binding syntax
Manipulate multiple inline style properties within a single binding
Implement conditional inline styles based on component state
Initialize and bind style properties from component class variables
Control style precedence by combining inline styles with other styling approaches
Construct responsive UI elements using inline style bindings

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core' to enable component creation and basic Angular directives.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Angular core features
import { Component, NgModule } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core imports are set up correctly for component creation.
successCriteria: Component and CommonModule are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator. Include the selector, template, and styles properties in the decorator configuration.
steps.hint: Remember to export the class and use the Component decorator imported in the previous step. The template can be a simple string for now.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create the AppComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator containing selector, template, and styles properties.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is exported and decorated with @Component containing selector, template, and styles properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've included all three properties (selector, template, styles) in the @Component decorator and exported the class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete. Check that you've created the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator containing selector, template, and styles properties.

steps.title: Add a basic heading element to the template
steps.instruction: Inside the @Component decorator, add a template property with an <h1> element containing the text 'Welcome to Inline Styles'.
steps.hint: The template property should be a string containing HTML. Add it after the selector property in the @Component decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template that displays a heading with the text 'Welcome to Inline Styles'.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with an <h1> element containing 'Welcome to Inline Styles'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the template property contains an <h1> element with the exact text 'Welcome to Inline Styles'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template property is missing or doesn't contain the required heading. Check that you've added the template property correctly.

steps.title: Apply inline style to the heading using style binding
steps.instruction: Add a style binding to the existing <h1> element to set its text color to blue using [style.color].
steps.hint: Use Angular's property binding syntax with square brackets around 'style.color' and set it to a string value like 'blue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: style binding for background color

Styled heading
steps.expectedOutcome: The heading text should appear in blue color when the application runs.
successCriteria: The <h1> element has [style.color] binding with value 'blue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct syntax: [style.color]="'blue'".
steps.feedbackWrong: The style binding wasn't added correctly. Check that you're using square brackets and the proper property name.

steps.instruction:
Add a paragraph element (

steps.hint: Use the [style.property] syntax for each style property you want to bind. Add the paragraph after the existing heading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of multiple style bindings on an element

Styled text
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a paragraph with two inline style bindings for font-size and font-weight.
successCriteria:
The template includes a

element with [style.font-size]="'18px'" and [style.font-weight]="'bold'" bindings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but it's missing one or both of the required style bindings. Make sure to include both [style.font-size] and [style.font-weight] bindings with the specified values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element with the required style bindings wasn't added correctly. Check that you're using the correct syntax for style binding and that both properties are included.

steps.title: Create a component property for dynamic styling
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, add a property named 'highlightColor' with type 'string' and initialize it with the value 'yellow'.
steps.hint: Define the property inside the class body, using TypeScript syntax: highlightColor: string = 'yellow';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a property that can be used to control inline styles dynamically.
successCriteria: AppComponent has a property named highlightColor with type string and initial value 'yellow'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the property is named 'highlightColor', has type 'string', and is initialized with 'yellow'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property wasn't added correctly. Check that it's defined inside the AppComponent class with the correct name, type, and initial value.

steps.title: Bind paragraph background color to the component property
steps.instruction: In the template, add a [style.background-color] binding to the paragraph element that references the 'highlightColor' property from the component class.
steps.hint: Use Angular's style binding syntax: [style.background-color]="highlightColor". This will apply the color value stored in the component property as the paragraph's background color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph element will have its background color dynamically controlled by the 'highlightColor' property value from the component class.
successCriteria: The paragraph element includes a [style.background-color] binding that references the 'highlightColor' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct syntax: [style.background-color]="highlightColor" on the paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element doesn't have the correct style binding. Remember to use [style.background-color]="highlightColor" to bind the background color to the component property.

steps.title: Add a button to change the highlight color
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template that, when clicked, updates the 'highlightColor' property to a new value (e.g., 'yellow').
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding to call a method that changes the property value. You can set the property directly in the template or create a method in the component class.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with click event
<button (click)="highlightColor = 'yellow'">Change Color</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that, when clicked, changes the highlightColor property value.
successCriteria: Button element is added to the template with a (click) event binding that updates the highlightColor property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has a (click) event binding that updates the highlightColor property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct event binding to update the highlightColor.

steps.title: Use ngStyle directive for multiple style bindings
steps.instruction: Add a <div> element with [ngStyle] binding that applies multiple styles from an object in the template.
steps.hint: Create a style object in the component class and bind it to a div using [ngStyle].
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with multiple styles applied via ngStyle directive appears in the template.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div> with [ngStyle] binding to a style object defined in the component class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the style object in the component class and the [ngStyle] binding in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a div with [ngStyle] binding. Check if you created a style object and bound it correctly.

steps.title: Create a method to return dynamic style object
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add a method named getDynamicStyles that returns an object with CSS style properties.
steps.hint: Define a method that returns an object like { 'font-size': '18px', 'padding': '10px' }. You can make some properties dynamic by using component properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that generates a style object, ready to be used with ngStyle binding.
successCriteria: AppComponent has a method named getDynamicStyles that returns an object with CSS style properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your method returns an object with CSS properties. Check that you're using the correct method name and return syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a method inside the AppComponent class that returns an object with style properties.
